palette.mood: A warm oxblood-brown seminar room (wall #2A140E, hue about 15 degrees, wood and wine, not plum) at late afternoon turning to dusk. The DiplomaPress is oxblood brass, the machine handle glows mint (#83D9B1, a cool with no green in it, clearly not 11-02's teal), paper is cream, highlighter yellow (#FFD23F) is the one warm LIGHT and the highlighter mark, and brass is a desaturated metal (#B08A4E).
palette.divergence: Against 11-02 (indigo, sodium amber, teal): this wall is a brown-red near hue 15 degrees, not indigo near 250, and the machine cool is mint near 210 not teal near 170. Against 10-29 (aubergine near 300): this wall is 285 degrees away on the wheel from violet. Against 11-01 (slate-green) and 10-31 (sage): no green anywhere.
palette.accent_licence: Mint ONLY on the machine handle, machine-written lines and the machine hand. The 119 student tags stay paper and get an mint underline tick only, so students are never coded as machines. Highlighter yellow ONLY as light and the highlight. Oxblood is the press body, the examiner handle and the human sleeve cuff. The human hand is skin (#C98F6B) at least two value steps from paper. Edit mark is ink. DROP stamp is ink at 60 percent. The 73 percent bar is chalk with an ink outline. The gavel is oak.

shape_language.grammar: RECTILINEAR against ROUND. Pages, tables, tags, flags, gauge, note card and the press are right angles. The only rounds are the question token and the ring of chairs, which is the token's circle at room scale ('who was asked' becomes a ring of seats).
shape_language.why: A plan is rectangles and the human question is round. The speech bubble is a square-cornered note card, the dial a rectilinear slide gauge and the map pins square flags, so the ring of chairs and the token are the only circles.
